probableRootCause: Mechanical seal degradation caused by dry-running conditions associated with suction cavitation, feed instability and insufficient seal flush.
physicalCause: Unstable suction conditions reduced reliable seal lubrication and cooling, while low seal flush flow increased the risk of seal damage.
detectionGap: Low seal flush flow did not have sufficient early warning and protective interlock coverage.
symptoms: Mechanical seal leakage developed during unstable operating conditions
Suction cavitation and feed swings were observed
Seal flush flow was insufficient
No adequate protective interlock was available for low seal flush flow

evidence.finding: Feed instability and suction cavitation created conditions associated with seal dry running.
Low seal flush flow reduced seal cooling and lubrication reliability.
Low seal flush condition lacked adequate alarm and interlock protection.

correctiveActions: Inspect and restore the mechanical seal system
preventiveActions: Install seal flush flow switch and DCS alarm
Implement protective interlock for low seal flush flow
Limit operating ramp rate to 1 T/H/min
proactiveActions: Roll out improved seal flush protection to similar pumps

probableRootCause: Bearing distress caused by degraded oil film due to water contamination in the lube oil system.
physicalCause: Water ingress into the lube oil through a leaking oil cooler tube.
detectionGap: Water contamination was not detected early because online water monitoring was not available.
symptoms: DE radial vibration increased from 28 micron to 52 micron before trip
Compressor tripped at 75 micron radial vibration
Lube oil water content reached 1800 ppm
Water content had exceeded the 500 ppm alarm threshold

evidence.finding: Radial vibration increased from 28 to 52 micron before reaching the 75 micron trip threshold.
Lube oil water content reached 1800 ppm compared with the 500 ppm alarm threshold.
Leaking cooler tube provided a credible water ingress path into the lube oil.
No online water monitoring was available for early detection.

correctiveActions: Repair the leaking oil cooler tube
Restore lube oil condition before equipment restart
preventiveActions: Install online lube oil water monitoring
Tighten vibration alert threshold to 45 micron
Monitor cooler differential pressure and conductivity
Strengthen periodic oil water and particle analysis
proactiveActions: Roll out the monitoring approach to KO-3202 and KO-3203

probableRootCause: Motor bearing overheating caused by degraded grease and an over-extended, non-risk-based relubrication interval.
physicalCause: Bearing lubrication condition deteriorated until friction and temperature increased.
detectionGap: Motor bearing temperature was not adequately trended and the routine vibration route did not sufficiently cover the motor.
symptoms: Motor bearing temperature increased from approximately 68°C to 84°C
Bearing grease condition was degraded
Relubrication interval was not sufficiently risk-based
Motor condition monitoring coverage was limited

evidence.finding: Motor bearing temperature increased from approximately 68°C to 84°C.
Inspection identified degraded bearing grease condition.
Existing relubrication frequency was insufficient for the observed operating condition.
Temperature trending and motor vibration monitoring coverage were insufficient for earlier detection.

preventiveActions: Revise motor bearing relubrication interval to four months
Implement motor bearing temperature trending and alerting
Include motors in monthly vibration monitoring
proactiveActions: Roll out improved motor bearing monitoring to similar equipment

event: High Fouling — Duty Loss & High dP
probableRootCause: Accelerated tube-side coke/polymer fouling associated with elevated heavy ends and insufficient fouling-based cleaning triggers.
physicalCause: Deposits accumulated on the tube side, increasing differential pressure and reducing heat-transfer duty.
detectionGap: No sufficiently defined differential-pressure cleaning trigger and fouling KPI were available for early intervention.
symptoms: Tube-side differential pressure increased
Heat-transfer duty decreased
Cold outlet temperature performance deteriorated
Heavy ends increased during the degradation period

evidence.finding: Increasing tube-side differential pressure was consistent with progressive fouling.
Heat exchanger duty declined as fouling progressed.
Elevated heavy ends increased the likelihood of coke/polymer deposit formation.
Cleaning decisions were not governed by a defined dP trigger and fouling performance KPI.

correctiveActions: Clean the exchanger and restore heat-transfer performance
preventiveActions: Establish differential-pressure cleaning trigger and alarm
Implement fouling-factor and heat-duty KPI monitoring
proactiveActions: Roll out fouling monitoring logic to similar heat exchangers

probableRootCause: Coupling misalignment aggravated by soft-foot condition and an aged coupling.
physicalCause: Mechanical misalignment generated elevated vibration, including increased 2X harmonic response.
detectionGap: Alignment verification was not included adequately in preventive maintenance and vibration monitoring frequency was too long for early detection.
symptoms: Overall vibration increased toward alarm and trip conditions
2X harmonic vibration increased
Coupling offset increased
Alignment condition deteriorated before intervention

evidence.finding: High vibration together with elevated 2X harmonic response was consistent with misalignment.
Coupling offset provided direct evidence of alignment degradation.
Soft-foot condition and coupling age increased susceptibility to misalignment.
Preventive alignment checks and vibration monitoring frequency were insufficient for earlier intervention.

preventiveActions: Add laser alignment and soft-foot checks to preventive maintenance
proactiveActions: Roll out alignment PM to other Class A blowers
Evaluate wireless vibration monitoring for critical blowers
